title: Why Airplane Windows Are Never Square
lines: Have you ever noticed that airplane windows are never square?
The first jet airliner, the de Havilland Comet, had nearly square openings in its body.
On every flight, the cabin is pressurized, and the metal skin stretches like a balloon.
At a sharp corner, all that stress piles up in one tiny spot.
Flight after flight, tiny cracks can start right there. In 1954, two Comets broke apart in the air.
A rounded window spreads the stress smoothly all the way around.
No sharp corner, no weak spot.
That's why airplane windows are rounded. Follow for more!
caption:
Airplane windows are rounded for a reason ✈️ In 1954, two de Havilland Comets — the first jet airliners — broke apart in flight. Investigators found metal-fatigue cracks at the corners of cut-outs in the cabin: every pressurized flight stretches the skin, and the stress piles up at sharp corners. Rounded windows spread it evenly.
